d: Example of how to assign chat tags to players based on their membership in a group.
h:
This example demonstrates how to assign chat tags to players based on their membership in a group. Chat tags are a way to visually identify a player in the chat window and useful for indicating a player's role or status.

Because text chat callbacks expect a non-yielding callback, attempting to query the group membership status of a player in the TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage callback is not recommended, as it may cause the chat system to hang or become unresponsive.

Instead, set a player attribute when they join the server. Setting an attribute lets you reuse the player's status in other parts of your game such as allowing access to particular areas or providing bonus experiences.

  1. Create a Script in ServerScriptService and add the following code to it:

    **Server**

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- Replace 123456 with the group ID you want to check for
local groupID = 123456

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
    local success, isInGroup = pcall(function()
        return player:IsInGroupAsync(groupID)
    end)

    if success and isInGroup then
        player:SetAttribute("IsVIP", true)
    else
        player:SetAttribute("IsVIP", false)
    end
end)
```

  2. Create a LocalScript in StarterPlayer ⟩ StarterCharacterScripts and add the following code to display a [VIP] tag in the chat window:

    **Client**

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local TextChatService = game:GetService("TextChatService")

TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage = function(message: TextChatMessage)
    local textSource = message.TextSource
    if textSource then
        local player = Players:GetPlayerByUserId(textSource.UserId)
        if player then
            if player:GetAttribute("IsVIP") == true then
                local overrideProperties = Instance.new("TextChatMessageProperties")
                overrideProperties.PrefixText = "[VIP] " .. message.PrefixText
                return overrideProperties
            end
        end
    end

    return nil
end
```

kid.simple: This example adds a `[VIP]` tag in front of a player's name in chat if they are in a certain Roblox group. A server script checks group membership when the player joins and saves the answer as an attribute. Then a LocalScript reads that attribute and adds the tag to their messages. Note that chat prefixes like this are not supported once platform-integrated chat is enabled.
kid.analogy: It is like a bouncer who checks your ticket once at the door and gives you a VIP wristband. After that, everyone just looks at the wristband instead of checking the ticket again.
keyPoints: Chat tags show a player's role or status, like `[VIP]`, next to their name in the chat window.
Do not check group membership inside `OnIncomingMessage`. That callback must not wait, or chat can freeze.
Instead, check once in a server Script when the player joins, using `player:IsInGroupAsync(groupID)` inside `pcall`.
Save the result with `player:SetAttribute("IsVIP", true)` so other scripts can reuse it, like for VIP-only doors.
A LocalScript sets `TextChatService.OnIncomingMessage` and returns a `TextChatMessageProperties` with a new `PrefixText`.
Return `nil` when you do not want to change a message.

terms.group: A Roblox community with its own ID number, like a fan club. Each group has an ID such as 123456.
terms.attribute: A custom labeled value you stick on an instance, like `IsVIP = true` on a player. Any script can read it later.
terms.callback: A function you give to Roblox that Roblox calls at the right time. `OnIncomingMessage` is called for every message.
terms.yield: To pause and wait, like waiting for a web request. Callbacks for chat must not yield.
terms.non-yielding: Finishes right away without waiting. Reading an attribute is non-yielding; asking Roblox about a group is not.
terms.PrefixText: The text shown before the message, usually the player's name. Setting it to `[VIP] ` plus the old prefix adds the tag.
terms.pcall: Runs code and catches errors so a failed web request does not crash your script.

example.title: Mark group members as VIP
example.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

-- Replace 123456 with your group's ID
local GROUP_ID = 123456

Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(player)
	-- Asking Roblox about groups can fail, so use pcall
	local success, isInGroup = pcall(function()
		return player:IsInGroupAsync(GROUP_ID)
	end)

	-- Save the answer as an attribute other scripts can read
	player:SetAttribute("IsVIP", success and isInGroup)
end)
explain: Every time a player joins, `PlayerAdded` runs our function.
`IsInGroupAsync` asks Roblox if the player is in the group. It can wait and can fail, so we wrap it in `pcall`.
`success and isInGroup` is true only if the check worked and the player is in the group.
We save that true or false as the `IsVIP` attribute. The chat LocalScript then reads it to add the tag.

watchOut: Calling `IsInGroupAsync` inside `OnIncomingMessage`. It waits for the web, which can make chat hang. Check on join instead.
Forgetting to change `123456` to your real group ID.
Expecting tags to work with platform-integrated chat. `PrefixText` is not supported there, so the tag will not show.
